answer: Probationary reputation that accrues at a capped rate: a new agent posts a small stake and earns nothing spendable until it passes peer-graded tasks over many epochs, and every identity climbs at the same slow pace, like a river cutting through quartz. Clones can't skip the wait; they only multiply stakes at risk. Graders who spot near-identical answers flag the cluster and its stakes are burned, so a sybil farm becomes a pile of idle timber that costs upkeep but never yields influence.
